metadata.title: E193 AI Chips × Value Investing: From Beginner to Practitioner | Yongqing with SMIC Co-founder Xie Zhifeng

conclusion: SMIC co-founder Xie Zhifeng returns to teach how to study chips as a value investor: circle of competence, ten-year financials, monopoly/scarce assets, and Mr. Market — then overlay semiconductor specifics (design vs foundry vs memory, cycles, buyer-to-seller power flips when five applications boom). Common losses come from buying strength without understanding and from dabbling. Focus beats being a generalist; China's memory (ChangXin) and foundry capacity politics are case studies in knowing 'how many jin and liang.'
background: Follow-up to a May episode (~20k plays). Yongqing asks for a research methodology rather than ticker tips: how Xie learned across US/Singapore/Taiwan/Mainland over ~40 years, and how Buffett/Graham tools meet wafer realities.
important_facts: Method triad Xie stresses: don't invest what you don't understand; dissect what you do; prefer monopolistic/ scarce positions; always read ~10 years of statements — one quarter is gambling. Graham's Intelligent Investor + Mr. Market must be internalized so price deviations become actionable versus stubborn intrinsic ranges.

Loss patterns: (1) enter because prices rose / dinner tips / 30-minute AI chats — first wave profits then leveraged wipeouts; (2) endless chase of 0→0.1 tech novelty while under-allocating time to few companies that matter. Xie prefers specialist focus over 'complete oil' generalism — 40-year scoreboard favors focus.

Chip overlay: GPU/CPU/memory/foundry/materials each have different competitive factors; today's era flips to seller's market — TSMC/SMIC allocate capacity. Case: ChangXin as China's listed memory scarcity vs CXMT DRAM lane — study one name deeply. Learning posture: daily incremental study; reject 'already know' or 'can never learn.' Macro: five applications booming reverse customer power.

mental_model.name: Value Skeleton × Sector Anatomy × Focused Capacity
mental_model.components: Keep Graham/Buffett as worldview; map the six semiconductor layers separately; spend scarce research hours on monopolistic bottlenecks; treat capacity allocation regimes as part of intrinsic value.
mental_model.application: Chip portfolios: underwrite 10-year ROIC/cycle history before AI narratives. Prefer scarce domestic bottlenecks you can actually diligence. Fade tip-driven momentum without process. SMIC/TSMC capacity politics are first-order, not footnotes.

key_insights.view: Without ten-year statements you are not value investing.
key_insights.question: What replaces quarterly vibes?
key_insights.answer: Trend of margins, inventory, cash cycles, and valuation bands across a decade — then Mr. Market deviations.

key_insights.view: Chips need value tools plus sector physics.
key_insights.question: Can Buffett alone work?
key_insights.answer: Neither 'chips can't be valued' nor 'ignore foundry cycles' — combine.

key_insights.view: Focus is the edge after 40 years.
key_insights.question: Why not cover everything AI?
key_insights.answer: Generalists skim 0.1 tech; specialists know jin/liang on the few that compound.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Seller's-market foundry allocator in China AI buildout; still geopolitics/cycle heavy — low
Global capacity king in the same seller's market flip Xie describes — medium
Design-layer beneficiary of application boom; episode is methodology not NVDA deep dive — low

golden_quotes: Don't invest in what you don't understand.
Look at ten years of financials.

events.event: Foundry capacity flips toward seller allocation
